author: Claude (English teacher role)
basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.

slides.1: Good morning, everyone. Today we look at United Nations SDG 9. It is a global plan. It helps countries build better factories and support new science.
slides.2: AI is changing science very fast. It also changes how we share ideas. But the quality of the answer depends on one thing: how we ask.
slides.3: Many science students use ChatGPT or Gemini. We fix lab reports with it. We read short summaries. We ask about hard homework. It is fast and easy.
slides.4: This tool is convenient. But some students give too little information. Then the AI writes boring, repeated text. People call this AI slop. It has no real value.
slides.5: Why does this happen? The AI does not understand your ideas. It only guesses the next word. It uses the words in your prompt. Few details bring wrong answers.
slides.6: A good prompt has four parts. Give a role. Give background facts. Give a clear goal. Give simple rules. Clear instructions bring much better answers.
slides.7: Clear writing matters in science. Good prompts help our lab reports. They also help our presentations. Our work becomes faster and more correct.
slides.8: But do not copy the answer without thinking. You will stop learning. Real science starts with human curiosity. It does not start with fast answers.
slides.9: So think before you type. Ask yourself one question. What do I really need? Who will read this? Which format is best for this task?
slides.10: Then give the AI clear instructions. Add your student background. Add the format you want. Prompt writing is science communication too.
slides.11: Computers organize data very well. But they have no curiosity. They have no intuition. They have no honest heart. People turn numbers into new discoveries.
slides.12: In conclusion, good innovation starts with good communication. Better prompts bring better answers. But scientists still think carefully every day. Thank you.
